items.title: Fed delivers surprise 50bp cut to 3.25%-3.50%
items.body: The Federal Reserve cut the federal funds target range by 50 basis points to 3.25%-3.50% on Wednesday, March 17, 2027. Fed funds futures had priced an 85% probability of a 25bp move going into the decision. The 2-year Treasury yield fell 17bp and the dollar index dropped 0.7% within minutes.

rationale: A larger-than-priced cut lowers the expected policy path, pulls down real yields and weakens the USD, cutting the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold.

items.title: Fed unexpectedly raises rates 25bp, citing re-acceleration in inflation
items.body: The FOMC raised its target range by 25bp to 4.00%-4.25% on June 16, 2027, a move only 8% of futures pricing had anticipated. The statement said inflation had 're-accelerated materially' and that further firming may be appropriate. The 2-year yield jumped 19bp and the dollar index rose 0.9%.

rationale: An unpriced hike with a tightening bias lifts real yields and the USD, raising the opportunity cost of gold.

items.title: Fed holds at 3.50%-3.75% as expected; statement and dots little changed
items.body: The Fed left rates unchanged at 3.50%-3.75% on January 27, 2027, as futures had fully priced. The statement was nearly word-for-word identical to December's, and the chair repeated that policy is 'well positioned' and decisions remain meeting-by-meeting. Treasury yields and the dollar were little changed after the release.

rationale: A fully priced hold with unchanged guidance delivers no new information to rate expectations, real yields or the USD, so there is no directional impulse for gold.

items.title: Fed cuts 25bp to 3.25%-3.50% as expected
items.body: The Federal Reserve lowered its policy range by 25bp to 3.25%-3.50% on September 22, 2027, a move fully priced by futures markets.

items.title: Fed dots signal just one more cut through 2028; four dissents
items.body: The updated Summary of Economic Projections shows the median official expects only one further 25bp cut by end-2028, versus three in the June projections, and raised the 2028 core PCE forecast to 2.8% from 2.5%. Four officials dissented in favour of holding rates. The 2-year yield rose 11bp and the dollar index gained 0.6% after the release.

rationale: The cut itself was priced; the hawkish dots and dissents raise the expected rate path, lifting real yields and the USD, which outweighs the priced cut for gold.

items.title: Fed holds, but dots now show three cuts in 2027
items.body: The Fed kept rates at 3.75%-4.00% on March 17, 2027, as expected. The median dot now shows three 25bp cuts in 2027 versus two in December, and the core PCE projection was lowered to 2.4% from 2.7%. The 2-year yield fell 9bp and the dollar index slipped 0.4%.

rationale: A dovish hold lowers the expected rate path, pushing down real yields and the USD, which supports gold despite no change in the current rate.

items.title: Fed hikes 25bp as expected but drops tightening bias
items.body: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 4.75%-5.00% on July 28, 2027, a move priced at about 90%. The statement removed the phrase 'additional policy firming may be appropriate' and replaced it with language about assessing 'the cumulative tightening of policy'. The chair said rates are 'at or near' their peak; the 2-year yield fell 8bp and the dollar weakened 0.5%.

rationale: A priced hike combined with removal of the tightening bias signals an end to the cycle, lowering expected rates and the USD; some analysts would treat the higher policy rate as an offset, hence a capped confidence.

items.title: Fed to slow balance-sheet runoff sooner than dealers expected
items.body: The Fed said on May 5, 2027, that it will reduce the monthly cap on Treasury runoff to $5 billion from $25 billion starting June 1, while leaving MBS runoff unchanged. The latest primary dealer survey had expected the slowdown in the third quarter. The 10-year term premium estimate fell about 4bp after the announcement.

rationale: An earlier QT slowdown modestly eases term premium and liquidity conditions, lowering long real yields; the effect on gold is small and second-order, so confidence is capped.

items.title: FOMC minutes: many officials open to further hikes if inflation stalls
items.body: Minutes of the Fed's April 27-28, 2027 meeting showed 'many participants' judged further policy firming could become appropriate if progress on inflation stalled, while 'some' saw a case for holding rates restrictive for longer. Markets had expected a balanced tone. The 2-year yield rose 6bp and the dollar index firmed 0.3%.

rationale: Hawkish-leaning minutes raise expected rates and the USD, lifting real yields and weighing on gold.

items.title: Fed governor backs rate cut at next meeting on labour softening
items.body: A Federal Reserve governor, a permanent FOMC voter, said on February 18, 2027, it would be 'appropriate to lower rates at our March meeting' as the labour market cools faster than expected. Futures-implied odds of a March cut rose to 65% from 40%. The dollar index eased 0.3%.

rationale: A voting governor explicitly endorsing a near-term cut raises cut odds, lowering yields and the USD, which supports gold.

items.title: Fed hawk repeats call for no cuts this year
items.body: A non-voting regional Fed president, long regarded as the committee's most hawkish member, said on October 6, 2027, that she sees 'no case for any rate cuts this year' and would favour a hike if core inflation stays above 3%. Her remarks repeated views she gave in three speeches over the past month. Fed funds futures pricing was unchanged after the comments.

rationale: Hawkish words from a known hawk without a vote, repeating prior views, carry no new information for rate expectations; futures did not move, so any impulse for gold via yields or the USD is negligible.

items.title: Futures price near-certain Fed cut this week
items.body: Fed funds futures on Monday, October 25, 2027, priced a 96% probability of a 25bp cut at Wednesday's FOMC decision, and a 70% probability of a further cut in December.

items.title: Fed cuts 25bp but signals pause with new 'extent and timing' language
items.body: The Fed cut rates 25bp to 3.00%-3.25% on October 27, 2027, as expected, but the statement added that in considering 'the extent and timing of additional adjustments' it would assess incoming data. The chair said the Fed is 'well positioned to wait'. December cut odds fell to 35% from 70%, the 2-year yield rose 10bp and the dollar gained 0.6%.

rationale: The cut was fully priced; the new guidance signalling a pause removes expected future easing, lifting front-end yields and the USD, which is bearish for gold.

items.title: Fed cuts 25bp; dots signal only one more cut in 2028
items.body: The Fed cut 25bp to 3.00%-3.25% on December 15, 2027, as expected, but the median dot now shows just one cut in 2028, versus two in September. The 2-year yield initially rose 7bp after the statement.

items.title: Chair says labour downside risks 'risen materially'; yields reverse
items.body: At the press conference the chair said downside risks to employment 'have risen materially' and that the dots 'are not a plan or a commitment'. The 2-year yield reversed to close 6bp lower on the day and the dollar index fell 0.4%.

rationale: Hawkish dots were overridden by a dovish press conference, and the market's net verdict was lower front-end yields and a weaker USD, mildly supportive of gold; conflicting signals justify capped confidence.

items.title: Fed adopts framework allowing inflation to run above 2% after shortfalls
items.body: The Fed concluded its framework review on August 27, 2027, adopting a flexible average-inflation-targeting approach under which it will aim for inflation moderately above 2% for some time after periods of undershooting. 10-year breakeven inflation rose 8bp while the 10-year TIPS real yield fell 6bp. The dollar index slipped 0.5%.

rationale: A more inflation-tolerant framework lowers real yields and the USD and raises inflation-hedge demand, all supportive of gold.

items.title: White House says President intends to remove Fed chair
items.body: The White House said on April 9, 2027, that the President intends to remove the Fed chair 'for cause' and will name a replacement who favours 'much lower rates'. The chair said in a statement she will not resign and that the law protects the Fed's independence. The dollar index fell 0.9%, 10-year breakevens rose 9bp and the 30-year Treasury yield rose 12bp.

rationale: A direct threat to Fed independence raises inflation and debasement risk premia and weakens the USD, driving safe-haven and inflation-hedge demand for gold even as long nominal yields rise.

items.title: US CPI jumps 0.6% in January, core 0.5%, both above forecasts
items.body: US consumer prices rose 0.6% in January 2027 versus a 0.3% consensus, the BLS said on February 10. Core CPI rose 0.5% against expectations of 0.3%, lifting the annual core rate to 3.4% from 3.1%. The 2-year Treasury yield jumped 14bp and the dollar rose 0.7%.

rationale: A broad hot inflation surprise pushes out expected Fed cuts, lifting real yields and the USD, which weighs on gold in the near term.

items.title: US payrolls fall 45,000; unemployment rises to 4.6%
items.body: US nonfarm payrolls fell by 45,000 in July 2027 versus a consensus gain of 150,000, the Labor Department said on August 6. The unemployment rate rose to 4.6% from 4.3%. Futures now price a 90% chance of a September Fed cut, up from 55%.

rationale: A sharp labour-market miss raises Fed cut expectations, lowering real yields and the USD, which supports gold.

items.title: US CPI rises 0.3% in May, in line; core also 0.3%
items.body: US CPI rose 0.3% in May 2027 and core CPI 0.3%, both exactly matching consensus, with annual rates of 2.9% and 3.0% also as forecast. Shelter and services components were in line with recent trends. Treasury yields and the dollar were little changed after the release.

rationale: An in-line print with no component surprise leaves rate expectations, real yields and the USD unchanged, giving no directional signal for gold.

items.title: US jobless claims surge to 291,000, highest since 2021
items.body: Initial jobless claims rose to 291,000 in the week ended March 13, 2027, from 231,000, versus expectations of 228,000, the Labor Department said. The department cited no holiday, weather or state-specific distortions. Continuing claims climbed to 2.05 million, and the 2-year yield fell 8bp.

rationale: A large, undistorted jump in claims signals labour-market weakening, raising cut expectations and lowering yields and the USD, which supports gold.

items.title: US CPI 0.5% on gasoline spike, but core rises just 0.1%
items.body: US headline CPI rose 0.5% in April 2027 against a 0.3% forecast, driven by a 9% jump in gasoline prices. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose only 0.1% versus the 0.3% consensus, its smallest gain in two years, with shelter up 0.2%. The 2-year yield fell 5bp after the release.

rationale: The Fed and markets key off core inflation; a soft core print lowers expected rates and yields despite an energy-driven headline beat, which is mildly supportive of gold, though the headline creates some offset.

items.title: US payrolls beat at 245,000, but jobless rate rises and wages soften
items.body: US nonfarm payrolls rose 245,000 in September 2027 versus a 160,000 forecast. However, the unemployment rate rose to 4.5% from 4.3% and average hourly earnings gained just 0.1% versus 0.3% expected.

items.title: Prior two months of payrolls revised down by 118,000
items.body: Revisions cut July and August payroll gains by a combined 118,000, lowering the three-month average to 104,000 from 141,000. After an initial rise, the 2-year yield traded 4bp lower within an hour of the release.

rationale: The headline beat is outweighed by a higher jobless rate, soft wages and heavy downward revisions, which together point to a cooling labour market and lower yields; the mixed report justifies a capped confidence.

items.title: US core PCE prices rise 0.4%, above 0.2% forecast
items.body: The core PCE price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, rose 0.4% in June 2027 versus a 0.2% consensus, lifting the annual rate to 3.0% from 2.8%, the Commerce Department said on July 30. Personal income and spending were in line with forecasts. The dollar index rose 0.4%.

rationale: A hot surprise in the Fed's preferred inflation gauge raises expected rates, real yields and the USD, weighing on gold.

items.title: US PPI jumps 0.5% on trade margins; PCE-linked components soft
items.body: US producer prices for final demand rose 0.5% in March 2027 versus a 0.2% forecast, driven mostly by a 1.8% rise in trade-services margins, one day after an in-line CPI. Components that feed the Fed's PCE gauge were soft: portfolio management fees fell 1.2%, airline fares fell 2.5% and physician care prices were flat. Several bank economists cut their core PCE estimate for March to 0.18% from 0.27%.

rationale: The headline beat is driven by volatile margins that do not feed PCE, while the PCE-relevant components imply a softer core PCE, lowering expected rates and supporting gold; a headline-reading reaction could briefly go the other way.

items.title: ISM manufacturing slumps to 46.8, new orders contract sharply
items.body: The ISM manufacturing index fell to 46.8 in February 2027 from 49.1, versus a 49.5 consensus, with new orders dropping to 44.1 and employment at 45.0.

items.title: ISM prices-paid index jumps to 69.4, highest since 2022
items.body: The survey's prices-paid component rose to 69.4 from 62.0, the highest since 2022, with respondents citing tariffs and freight costs. The 10-year Treasury yield fell 4bp on the day.

rationale: The growth miss lowers yields and raises cut expectations (supportive), while the price spike is an inflation warning (negative); the net yield move favours mildly higher gold, with capped confidence.

items.title: US retail sales surge 1.3% in October, control group up 1.0%
items.body: US retail sales rose 1.3% in October 2027, well above the 0.4% forecast, and the control group used in GDP calculations climbed 1.0% versus 0.3% expected. September's figures were revised higher. The 2-year yield rose 9bp and the dollar gained 0.5%.

rationale: Broad consumer strength reduces expected Fed easing, lifting real yields and the USD, which weighs on gold.

items.title: US retail sales rise 1.1%, lifted by 5.8% jump in auto sales
items.body: US retail sales rose 1.1% in May 2027 versus a 0.5% forecast, with motor vehicle sales up 5.8% ahead of announced price increases.

items.title: Retail control group falls 0.3%; prior month revised lower
items.body: The control group, which excludes autos, gasoline, building materials and food services, fell 0.3% versus a 0.4% expected gain, and April's control reading was revised to -0.2% from +0.3%. Economists trimmed second-quarter consumption forecasts and the 2-year yield fell 5bp.

rationale: The headline beat comes from pulled-forward auto purchases, while the control group that drives GDP is weak and revised down; lower growth and yields are mildly supportive of gold, with capped confidence given the headline.

items.title: US core CPI rises 0.5%, above 0.3% forecast
items.body: US core CPI rose 0.5% in August 2027, above the 0.3% consensus, with services excluding housing up 0.7%. The headline index rose 0.4% versus 0.3% expected.

items.title: Jobless claims fall to 198,000, lowest in two years
items.body: Initial jobless claims fell to 198,000 in the same week's release versus 220,000 expected. The 2-year yield rose 15bp on the day and the dollar index climbed 0.8%.

rationale: Hot inflation and a tight labour market both push Fed easing expectations out, lifting real yields and the USD, which is bearish for gold.

items.title: BLS preliminary benchmark cuts payroll level by 910,000
items.body: The BLS preliminary annual benchmark revision, released August 25, 2027, showed nonfarm payroll employment for March 2027 was 910,000 lower than previously reported, versus expectations of about 500,000. Economists said monthly job growth over the period was overstated by roughly 75,000 a month. Fed funds futures added about 8bp of easing through year-end.

rationale: A larger-than-expected downward benchmark revision signals a weaker labour market and modestly raises cut expectations, lowering yields; it is backward-looking, so the effect on gold is mild and confidence is capped.

items.title: US core CPI in line at 0.3%, but 'supercore' services jump 0.7%
items.body: US core CPI rose 0.3% in November 2027, matching forecasts, but services excluding housing, the 'supercore' measure watched by the Fed, rose 0.7%, the largest gain in two years. A soft 0.1% shelter reading held the core figure down. The 2-year yield rose 5bp after the release.

rationale: The in-line core masks hot services inflation the Fed watches closely, nudging yields and the USD higher, which is mildly bearish for gold; the in-line headline core limits conviction.

items.title: Dollar index slides 1.2% to 97.10 in broad selloff
items.body: The dollar index fell 1.2% to 97.10 on May 12, 2027, its biggest one-day drop in a year, as the euro and yen rallied on reports that several reserve managers were reducing dollar allocations. The dollar fell against all G10 currencies.

rationale: Gold is priced in USD; a broad dollar decline makes gold cheaper for non-USD buyers and mechanically lifts XAUUSD.

items.title: 10-year TIPS real yield jumps 21bp to 2.45%
items.body: The 10-year Treasury inflation-protected real yield rose 21bp to 2.45% on September 9, 2027, its highest since 2008, after strong services data and hawkish Fed commentary. The nominal 10-year yield rose 18bp to 4.86% and the dollar index gained 0.6%.

rationale: Higher real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold and coincide with a firmer USD, a classic bearish combination for gold.

items.title: ECB holds deposit rate at 2.00%, as expected
items.body: The European Central Bank kept its deposit rate at 2.00% on June 10, 2027, as unanimously expected by economists. The ECB President repeated that decisions remain data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting, and staff projections were little changed. EUR/USD was flat after the decision.

rationale: A fully expected ECB hold with unchanged guidance does not move EUR/USD or global yields, so there is no impulse for gold via the USD.

items.title: BoJ surprises with hike to 1.00%, signals more to come
items.body: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate 25bp to 1.00% on April 28, 2027, a move markets had priced at about 20%, and said further hikes would follow if its outlook is realised. USD/JPY fell 2.1% to 148.10 and the dollar index fell 0.5%. The 10-year JGB yield rose 9bp, and US 10-year yields rose 3bp in sympathy.

rationale: A hawkish BoJ surprise strengthens the yen and weakens the USD, mildly supporting XAUUSD; spillover to higher global yields and potential carry-unwind deleveraging partly offset, so confidence is capped.

items.title: Yen surges in suspected intervention; USD/JPY drops from 161.9 to 155.3
items.body: USD/JPY plunged from 161.90 to 155.30 within an hour during Tokyo trading on July 14, 2027, in what traders described as suspected Japanese intervention. The dollar index fell 0.8%.

items.title: Japan confirms yen intervention; Treasury yields edge up
items.body: Japan's top currency diplomat confirmed later in the day that authorities had intervened and said they stand ready to act again. US 10-year Treasury yields rose 4bp on speculation that Japan funded the intervention by selling Treasuries.

rationale: The intervention weakens the USD, which supports XAUUSD, but the effect is partly offset by higher US yields from reserve selling, and intervention effects often fade, so confidence is capped.

items.title: SNB cuts to -0.25%, pledges FX intervention
items.body: The Swiss National Bank cut its policy rate 25bp to -0.25% on March 25, 2027, against expectations of a hold, and said it was willing to intervene in currency markets. EUR/CHF rose 1.2% and USD/CHF rose 1.4%. The dollar index was up 0.1%, as the franc has no weight in the index.

rationale: The SNB move affects the franc but barely moves the dollar index or US real yields, the main drivers of XAUUSD; negative Swiss rates could marginally support gold demand from Swiss investors, but the USD-terms effect is negligible.

items.title: PBoC sets weakest yuan fixing in years; Shanghai gold premium jumps
items.body: The People's Bank of China set the USD/CNY midpoint at 7.3520 on August 11, 2027, far weaker than the 7.2910 analyst estimate, a signal of tolerance for depreciation amid tariff pressure. The offshore yuan fell 1.1% and the dollar index rose 0.4%. The Shanghai Gold Exchange premium over London jumped to $38 an ounce from $8 as local investors sought to hedge currency weakness.

expected.second_label: disputed: second=NEUTRAL (stronger USD vs surge in Chinese hedging demand)

rationale: A modestly stronger USD is a headwind, but yuan devaluation drives Chinese capital-flight and hedging demand for gold, visible in the surging local premium, and raises global risk aversion; the channels conflict, so confidence is capped.

items.title: Weak 10-year auction tails 3.4bp; yields jump
items.body: A $42 billion US 10-year note auction on February 9, 2027, tailed by 3.4bp, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.21, the lowest since 2009, and indirect bidders taking 58% versus a 70% average. The 10-year yield rose 9bp to 4.92% and the dollar index rose 0.3%.

rationale: A poor auction lifts yields and the USD near term, raising gold's opportunity cost; fiscal-sustainability concern can support gold over longer horizons, so confidence is capped.

items.title: Treasury keeps coupon sizes unchanged, leans on bills
items.body: The US Treasury said in its quarterly refunding statement on May 5, 2027, that it expects to keep nominal coupon auction sizes unchanged 'for at least the next several quarters' and will meet financing needs with increased bill issuance. Primary dealers had expected coupon increases starting in August. The 10-year yield fell 8bp and term premium estimates declined.

rationale: Less duration supply than expected lowers long-end yields and term premium, reducing gold's opportunity cost; the channel is indirect, so confidence is capped.

items.title: ECB surprises with 50bp cut; euro drops 1%
items.body: The ECB cut its deposit rate by 50bp to 1.50% on November 4, 2027, versus a 25bp consensus, citing a sharp deterioration in euro-area growth. EUR/USD fell 1.0% to 1.0710.

items.title: BoE unexpectedly cuts rates; sterling slides
items.body: Hours later the Bank of England cut Bank Rate 25bp to 3.25%, a move economists had not expected until December. GBP/USD fell 0.9% and the dollar index rose 0.8% on the day.

rationale: Dovish surprises from the ECB and BoE strengthen the USD, mechanically weighing on XAUUSD; global easing is supportive of gold in other currencies and over time, so confidence is capped.

items.title: US 10-year yield drops 15bp; real yields fall
items.body: The 10-year Treasury yield fell 15bp to 4.05% on June 23, 2027, while the 10-year TIPS real yield fell 12bp to 1.72%.

items.title: Dollar index falls 0.8%
items.body: The dollar index fell 0.8% to 98.40 on the same day, its third straight decline.

rationale: Falling real yields and a weaker USD are the two strongest macro tailwinds for gold, and both point in the same direction.

items.title: 10-year yield rises 10bp, driven entirely by breakevens
items.body: The US 10-year nominal yield rose 10bp to 4.60% on March 3, 2027, but the move was driven entirely by a 12bp rise in 10-year breakeven inflation after an oil supply shock, while the 10-year TIPS real yield fell 2bp to 2.03%. The dollar index was unchanged.

rationale: Gold keys off real rather than nominal yields; rising inflation expectations with slightly lower real yields and a flat USD are mildly supportive, despite a headline rise in nominal yields.

items.title: Iran fires ballistic missiles at Israeli cities after strike on nuclear site
items.body: Iran launched dozens of ballistic missiles at Israeli cities on May 2, 2027, hours after an airstrike on one of its nuclear facilities, and Israel vowed a 'decisive' response. Brent crude jumped 8% to $91 a barrel and S&P 500 futures fell 2%. Treasury yields fell 7bp.

rationale: A sharp military escalation in a major oil region drives safe-haven demand for gold, reinforced by lower Treasury yields.

items.title: Israel and Iran agree ceasefire after six-week war
items.body: Israel and Iran agreed to a comprehensive ceasefire effective at midnight on July 8, 2027, ending a six-week conflict during which gold had gained about 6%, mediators said. Both governments confirmed the agreement. Brent fell 5%, equity futures rose 1.5% and Treasury yields rose 5bp.

rationale: A confirmed ceasefire removes the geopolitical risk premium built into gold during the conflict, reducing safe-haven demand.

items.title: US announces 30% tariffs on EU and Japan, 60% on China
items.body: The US administration announced on April 2, 2027, tariffs of 30% on all imports from the EU and Japan and 60% on imports from China, effective in 14 days, well above levels flagged by officials.

items.title: EU and China unveil retaliation; stocks slide, yields fall
items.body: The EU and China announced retaliation lists covering $310 billion of US goods within hours. S&P 500 futures fell 2.5%, the 10-year Treasury yield fell 9bp on growth fears, and economists raised US recession probabilities.

rationale: A trade-war escalation raises stagflation and recession risk, lowers yields and spurs safe-haven and reserve-diversification demand for gold.

items.title: US and China agree 90-day tariff truce, cutting duties sharply
items.body: The US and China agreed on September 13, 2027, to cut reciprocal tariffs to 30% from 125% for 90 days while talks continue, a deeper reduction than expected. Global equities rallied about 3%, the 10-year Treasury yield rose 10bp and the dollar index gained 1%.

rationale: De-escalation reduces safe-haven demand and lifts yields and the USD, a bearish mix for gold.

items.title: G7 agrees to confiscate frozen Russian central bank assets
items.body: G7 leaders agreed on June 14, 2027, to confiscate, rather than just freeze, about $280 billion of Russian central bank assets to fund Ukraine. Officials from several emerging-market central banks told reporters they were reviewing where their reserves are held.

rationale: Confiscating sovereign reserves heightens the perceived risk of holding Western-custodied assets, supporting official-sector diversification into gold; the near-term price effect may be modest, so confidence is capped.

items.title: Tanker traffic through Strait of Hormuz halted after seizures, mine reports
items.body: Iran-backed forces seized two tankers and naval officials reported mines in the Strait of Hormuz on October 19, 2027, halting commercial transits through the chokepoint that carries about a fifth of global oil.

items.title: Brent jumps 14%; stocks fall
items.body: Brent crude jumped 14% to $98 a barrel, US 10-year breakevens rose 9bp and the S&P 500 fell 1.8%.

rationale: A major shipping-lane disruption drives safe-haven demand, and the oil-driven rise in inflation expectations adds hedge demand for gold.

items.title: Report: Russia and Ukraine in secret ceasefire talks
items.body: A news report citing two unnamed sources said on March 3, 2027, that Russian and Ukrainian officials had held secret ceasefire talks in Istanbul. Gold fell 0.8% on the report.

items.title: Kremlin and Kyiv deny ceasefire talks report
items.body: About two hours later, the Kremlin spokesman called the report 'a fabrication' and a senior Ukrainian official said no talks were planned. Gold recovered most of its losses.

rationale: An unconfirmed de-escalation rumour was quickly denied by both sides, leaving the geopolitical risk premium broadly unchanged; the net effect on safe-haven demand is roughly zero.

items.title: Military officers seize power in Mali; junta says mines unaffected
items.body: Military officers seized power in Mali on August 4, 2027, dissolving the transitional government. The junta said mining operations would continue normally. Mali accounts for roughly 2% of global mined gold supply.

rationale: A coup in a small producer has no material effect on global risk sentiment, the USD or real yields, and mine supply is a tiny share of the above-ground gold stock, so the effect on XAUUSD is negligible.

items.title: Iran launches telegraphed retaliatory strike; most missiles intercepted
items.body: Iran launched a retaliatory missile and drone strike on an Israeli air base on November 10, 2027, an attack Iranian officials had signalled for days. Most projectiles were intercepted and no casualties were reported.

items.title: Iran says 'matter concluded'; Israel signals no immediate response
items.body: Iran's foreign minister said the matter was 'concluded' unless Iran is attacked again, and Israeli officials signalled no immediate response. Brent fell 5% and equity futures rose.

rationale: The strike was priced in and limited, and signals of no further escalation unwind the risk premium, a 'sell the news' outcome for safe-haven demand; residual tension keeps confidence capped.

items.title: China launches blockade drills around Taiwan; US sends carriers
items.body: China announced three days of live-fire blockade drills encircling Taiwan on April 20, 2027, and the US dispatched two carrier strike groups to the region. Asian equities fell 2-3% and the Taiwan dollar dropped 2%.

rationale: A major-power military standoff drives safe-haven demand for gold.

items.title: Peace talks collapse as delegations walk out
items.body: Talks aimed at ending the Russia-Ukraine war collapsed in Geneva on September 2, 2027, with mediators saying both delegations walked out. Markets had priced a high chance of a framework deal this month. European equities fell 1.5%.

rationale: Collapse of talks that markets expected to succeed restores the geopolitical risk premium, supporting safe-haven demand for gold.

items.title: Congress fails to raise debt limit; Treasury warns X-date ten days away
items.body: The US House failed on July 21, 2027, to pass a debt-limit increase, and the Treasury warned it could exhaust extraordinary measures in about ten days. One-month T-bill yields jumped 60bp and US credit default swap spreads widened to a record.

rationale: A potential US default undermines confidence in Treasuries and the USD, boosting safe-haven demand for gold; dollar-funding stress could briefly offset, so confidence is capped.

items.title: PBoC pauses gold buying after 18 straight months
items.body: The People's Bank of China reported gold reserves unchanged at 2,350 tonnes at end-May 2027, the first month without an addition after 18 consecutive months of purchases, data released June 7 showed. Analysts cited record-high prices as a likely reason.

rationale: A pause by a major official buyer removes a key source of price-insensitive demand and dents sentiment; the official channel is slow-moving, so the near-term effect is modest.

items.title: Central banks bought record 320 tonnes in Q3, WGC says
items.body: Central banks bought a record 320 tonnes of gold in the third quarter of 2027, bringing year-to-date purchases to 850 tonnes, the World Gold Council said on October 29. Much of the buying had already been reported in monthly IMF and central bank data.

expected.second_label: disputed: second=NEUTRAL (record CB buying but largely already reported)

rationale: Strong official-sector demand is supportive, but the quarterly report is backward-looking and partly known, so the near-term effect is small.

items.title: Gold ETFs see biggest weekly inflow in two years
items.body: Global gold-backed ETFs added 42 tonnes in the week to February 19, 2027, the largest weekly inflow in two years, including an 18-tonne single-day addition to the largest US fund.

rationale: Large ETF inflows reflect strong investment demand and directly absorb physical metal, supporting prices and momentum.

items.title: Gold ETFs shed 60 tonnes in a week
items.body: Global gold ETFs lost 60 tonnes in the week to August 13, 2027, including 22 tonnes from the largest US fund over three sessions, the biggest outflow since 2022.

rationale: Heavy ETF outflows signal waning investment demand and release metal into the market, weighing on prices.

items.title: India halves gold import duty to 3%
items.body: India cut its gold import duty to 3% from 6% in the budget on February 1, 2027, to curb smuggling. Jewellers said lower local prices would boost volumes ahead of the wedding season. Domestic gold futures fell 3% on the announcement.

rationale: A duty cut lowers local prices and should lift Indian physical demand, mildly supportive of global prices; the fall is in domestic futures, not XAUUSD, and the global effect is gradual.

items.title: India doubles gold import duty to 12% to curb deficit
items.body: India raised its gold import duty to 12% from 6% on September 3, 2027, to curb a widening current-account deficit. Local dealers said demand would weaken and domestic premiums flipped to discounts.

rationale: A sharp duty hike reduces demand from the second-largest consumer market, mildly bearish for global prices; the physical channel works gradually.

items.title: China allows insurers to invest in gold
items.body: China's financial regulator on March 8, 2027, allowed ten large insurers to invest up to 1% of total assets in gold in a pilot programme. Analysts estimated potential demand of about 200 tonnes.

rationale: Opening a large new institutional channel adds meaningful incremental investment demand for gold.

items.title: Strike halts output at large South African gold mine
items.body: Workers at a large South African gold mine producing about 1.1 million ounces a year went on strike on May 18, 2027, halting output. Global mine production is about 3,600 tonnes a year.

rationale: The mine produces about 1% of annual supply, which is tiny against the above-ground stock; gold prices are driven by investment and macro factors, not mine supply.

items.title: CME raises COMEX gold margins 18%, second hike in two weeks
items.body: CME Group said on October 15, 2027, it will raise maintenance margins on COMEX gold futures by 18% effective Monday, following several days of moves exceeding 3%. It was the exchange's second gold margin increase in two weeks.

rationale: Higher margins force leveraged longs to post more collateral or cut positions, a liquidity-driven selling pressure that often cools rallies; it does not change fundamentals, so confidence is capped.

items.title: China gold premium flips to $22 discount
items.body: Chinese gold traded at a $22 an ounce discount to London prices in the week to June 25, 2027, the weakest since 2020, as record prices hurt jewellery and bar demand.

items.title: Indian dealers offer discounts up to $45
items.body: Indian dealers offered discounts of up to $45 an ounce, the widest in a year, as buyers delayed purchases ahead of the monsoon off-season.

rationale: Discounts in the two largest consumer markets show weak physical demand, a mildly bearish signal; physical demand is a weak short-term driver, so confidence is capped.

items.title: Indian Dhanteras gold sales rise 25%
items.body: Indian jewellers' association said gold sales by volume during Dhanteras on October 28, 2027, rose about 25% from a year earlier, and dealers estimate October imports at 110 tonnes. Festival buying is a recurring seasonal pattern.

expected.second_label: disputed: second=NEUTRAL (seasonal festival buying, modest surprise)

rationale: Strong festival demand is mildly supportive via physical demand, but it is seasonal and largely expected, so its effect on XAUUSD is small.

items.title: Turkey's central bank sold 25 tonnes of gold to support lira
items.body: Turkey's central bank sold 25 tonnes of gold in March 2027 to support the lira, monthly reserve data showed on April 30.

items.title: Poland's central bank buys 30 tonnes, targets 30% gold share
items.body: Poland's central bank said the same day it bought 30 tonnes in the first quarter and plans to raise gold to 30% of its reserves.

rationale: Tactical selling by one central bank is roughly offset by strategic buying by another; the net official-sector signal is small, with a slight positive tilt from Poland's stated long-term plan.

items.title: FDIC seizes $180 billion regional lender after deposit run
items.body: US regulators seized a regional bank with $180 billion of assets on March 12, 2027, after a run on uninsured deposits. The KBW bank index fell 9%, the 2-year Treasury yield fell 28bp and futures raised the odds of a Fed cut at the next meeting.

rationale: Banking stress drives safe-haven demand and sharply lowers rate expectations and yields, both supportive of gold.

items.title: Stocks crash 8.5%; VIX hits 72 as margin calls spread
items.body: The S&P 500 fell 8.5% on October 18, 2027, its worst day since 1987, and the VIX hit 72. Credit markets froze and prime brokers issued widespread margin calls to hedge funds.

items.title: Gold drops 3.8% as investors sell winners to raise cash
items.body: Spot gold fell 3.8% intraday as investors sold liquid, profitable positions to meet margin calls. The dollar index jumped 1.5% and cross-currency basis swaps widened sharply, a sign of dollar-funding stress.

rationale: In a 'dash for cash', gold is sold to meet margin calls and the USD surges on funding stress, so the near-term effect is negative despite risk-off; a policy response could reverse it, so confidence is capped.

items.title: S&P downgrades US to AA, citing deficits and governance
items.body: S&P Global Ratings downgraded the US to AA from AA+ on August 6, 2027, citing persistent deficits and governance concerns. The 30-year Treasury yield rose 8bp and the dollar index fell 0.6%.

rationale: A sovereign downgrade dents confidence in US assets and the USD, supporting gold as an alternative reserve asset; higher long-end yields partly offset, so confidence is capped.

items.title: Fed launches unlimited repo and expands dollar swap lines
items.body: The Fed on March 16, 2027, announced unlimited daily repo operations and expanded dollar swap lines with five major central banks after SOFR spiked 50bp above interest on reserves. Funding spreads began to narrow within hours.

rationale: Emergency liquidity eases funding stress, which ends forced selling of gold, and expands the Fed balance sheet, both supportive; risk-on relief could reduce haven demand, so confidence is capped.

items.title: $60 billion private credit fund gates redemptions; spreads widen
items.body: A $60 billion private credit fund gated investor redemptions on June 8, 2027, the second such move by a major manager this month. US high-yield spreads widened 75bp, bank stocks fell 5% and the 10-year Treasury yield fell 10bp.

rationale: A credit event raises systemic-risk concern and lowers yields, supporting safe-haven demand; it is not yet a liquidity crunch that forces gold selling, but contagion could change that, so confidence is capped.

items.title: S&P 500 falls 4.2%; VIX jumps to 38
items.body: The S&P 500 fell 4.2% on February 24, 2027, and the VIX jumped to 38. Treasuries rallied, with the 2-year yield down 20bp as traders bet on Fed cuts, and the dollar index fell 0.4%.

rationale: A sharp equity selloff without funding stress drives safe-haven demand and lowers yields and the USD, all supportive of gold.

items.title: Global markets crash; gold falls 4.5% on margin-call selling
items.body: Global equities crashed on November 15, 2027, with the S&P 500 down 7%, and spot gold fell 4.5% as funds sold liquid assets to meet margin calls. The dollar index rose 1.3%.

items.title: Fed cuts 50bp in emergency move, launches liquidity backstops
items.body: Before the open on November 16, the Fed cut rates 50bp in an emergency intermeeting move, announced unlimited repo operations and activated swap lines with six central banks. Equity futures stabilised and the dollar index fell 1.2%.

rationale: Day 1 liquidation drove gold lower, but the emergency cut and backstops lower yields, weaken the USD and end forced selling, so the forward direction is up; volatile conditions cap confidence.

items.title: Troubled bank acquired over weekend with government guarantee
items.body: A troubled US bank was acquired by a larger rival over the weekend of April 10-11, 2027, with a government loss-sharing guarantee, and deposit outflows halted. Bank stocks rose 6% in Monday pre-market trading and the 2-year Treasury yield rose 15bp as traders pared Fed cut bets.

rationale: Resolution of bank stress reduces safe-haven demand, and higher yields from reduced cut bets weigh on gold; residual concerns about the banking system cap confidence.

items.title: 30-year Treasury yield jumps 38bp in two days on basis-trade unwind
items.body: The 30-year Treasury yield rose 38bp over April 8-9, 2027, as hedge funds unwound leveraged basis trades and swap spreads collapsed to record lows.

items.title: Dollar falls 1.9% as investors 'sell America'
items.body: Over the same two days the dollar index fell 1.9% and the S&P 500 fell 5%, with strategists citing a 'sell America' trade as foreign investors cut US assets.

rationale: Rising yields alone would weigh on gold, but here yields rise alongside a falling USD and equities, signalling an erosion of confidence in US assets that drives demand for gold; deleveraging could cause temporary selling, so confidence is capped.

items.title: Nasdaq drops 6.1% in AI tech selloff; VIX doubles
items.body: The Nasdaq Composite fell 6.1% on July 21, 2027, led by megacap AI stocks, and the VIX rose to 32 from 15. The 10-year Treasury yield fell 12bp and the dollar index slipped 0.5%.

rationale: Risk-off with falling yields and a softer USD supports gold via safe-haven demand and lower opportunity cost; no funding stress is reported.

items.title: Fed holds rates steady at 4.00-4.25%, as expected
items.body: The Federal Reserve left its policy rate unchanged at 4.00-4.25% on Wednesday, a decision fully priced by fed funds futures for weeks. The statement was nearly identical to the previous one and the vote was unanimous. The committee repeated that future moves will depend on incoming data.

rationale: A fully priced hold with an unchanged statement carries no surprise for yields or the dollar, so there is no news-driven impulse for gold.

items.title: US CPI rises 0.3% in March, matching forecasts
items.body: US consumer prices rose 0.3% m/m in March, in line with the 0.3% consensus, and 2.8% y/y versus 2.8% expected. Core CPI also rose 0.3% m/m as forecast. Two-year Treasury yields were little changed in the minutes after the release.

rationale: Headline and core CPI exactly matched consensus and front-end yields did not move, so rate expectations and gold are unaffected.

items.title: ECB trims deposit rate to 1.75% in widely flagged move
items.body: The European Central Bank cut its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 1.75%, a move policymakers had signalled at the April meeting and money markets had fully priced. President Lagarde said decisions remain meeting-by-meeting. The euro was flat against the dollar.

rationale: A fully priced ECB cut left EUR/USD flat, so there is no dollar channel to move gold.

items.title: Fed cuts by 25 bp, in line with report from last week
items.body: The Federal Reserve lowered its target range by 25 basis points to 3.50-3.75%, the exact outcome reported by a financial newspaper eight days earlier citing officials. Futures had assigned a 97% probability to the move. The median projection still shows two more cuts in 2028, unchanged from June. Spot gold had climbed about 5% in the two weeks leading into the meeting on expectations of the cut.

rationale: The cut was leaked, fully priced and the projections were unchanged, so there is no new dovish information; after a 5% pre-meeting run-up a sell-the-fact dip is plausible, hence NEUTRAL or mild DOWN at low confidence.

items.title: China's retaliation smaller than feared: 5% tariffs on US farm goods
items.body: Beijing announced 5% tariffs on $18 billion of US agricultural imports in response to new US levies, far short of the broad 25% retaliation that analysts had warned of last week. Officials also said talks would resume next month. S&P 500 futures rose 1.2% while the yen and Swiss franc weakened.

rationale: A smaller-than-feared shock is a relief event: risk appetite improves and safe havens (yen, franc, gold) lose some premium, but the move is modest.

items.title: US adds 172,000 jobs in October, close to forecasts
items.body: Nonfarm payrolls rose 172,000 in October against a consensus of 170,000, and the unemployment rate held at 4.2% as expected. Average hourly earnings rose 0.3% m/m, matching forecasts, and prior-month revisions were negligible.

rationale: Payrolls, unemployment and wages all matched consensus with no revisions, so Fed pricing and gold are unaffected.

items.title: China's central bank extends gold buying to 18th month
items.body: The People's Bank of China said its gold holdings rose by 5 tonnes in June, its 18th consecutive monthly increase. The figure matched the pace of the previous five months and the amount already estimated by customs-flow trackers last week. Officials gave no indication of a change in reserve strategy.

rationale: Official-sector buying is structurally supportive, but this print repeats a known pace already estimated by trackers, so it adds little near-term demand surprise.

items.title: Israel strikes Iranian military sites in limited, long-telegraphed response
items.body: Israel carried out strikes on several Iranian air-defence sites overnight, an operation officials in Washington had previewed publicly for a week. The strikes avoided oil and nuclear facilities, and Iranian state media played down the damage, saying no further response was planned. Brent crude fell 3% in Asian trading.

rationale: The strike was pre-announced and contained, and Iran signalled no retaliation, so the geopolitical risk premium built in advance tends to unwind (oil falling confirms de-escalation).

items.title: US Treasury warns of larger auctions ahead
items.body: The US Treasury kept nominal coupon auction sizes unchanged for the coming quarter, as primary dealers had unanimously forecast. Its statement again said it anticipates 'considering future increases' in coupon sizes, wording identical to the previous three refunding statements. Ten-year yields were 1 basis point lower after the release.

rationale: The refunding matched dealer forecasts and the forward guidance was copied from prior statements, so there is no term-premium or yield shock for gold despite the alarming headline.

items.title: Fed cuts 25 bp; new dots show three cuts next year, up from two
items.body: The Federal Reserve cut rates by 25 basis points as fully expected. The updated median projection now shows three cuts in 2028, up from two in the June projections, matching the three cuts already priced in fed funds futures before the meeting. The chair said the committee was 'not on a preset course'. Two-year yields ended the session 2 basis points higher.

rationale: The dots became more dovish only relative to old projections; they merely converged on what futures already priced, and front-end yields barely moved, so there is no dovish surprise for gold.

items.title: Fed's Harlow: no rush to cut rates
items.body: Federal Reserve Governor Ellen Harlow said on Tuesday there is 'no rush' to lower interest rates, citing services inflation that remains well above target. She said current policy is 'appropriately restrictive' and could stay there 'for some time'. Fed funds futures trimmed the odds of a June cut to 35% from 55%.

rationale: Hawkish Fed guidance pushed cut odds lower, lifting yields and the dollar and raising the opportunity cost of holding gold.

items.title: US hiring surges in June as payrolls blow past forecasts
items.body: Nonfarm payrolls rose 48,000 in June, well below the 185,000 economists expected, and the prior two months were revised down by a combined 71,000. The unemployment rate rose to 4.6% from 4.4%. Fed funds futures moved to price a near-certain September cut.

rationale: The headline is wrong: the body shows a large miss with downward revisions and rising unemployment, which lowers yields via dovish repricing and supports gold.

items.title: Russia's central bank denies plans to sell gold reserves
items.body: The Bank of Russia on Thursday denied a newspaper report that it was preparing to sell part of its gold reserves to cover a budget shortfall, calling the report 'without foundation'. The bank said its reserve management approach is unchanged. The original report had been published hours earlier and was not picked up widely.

rationale: The denial restores the status quo and the original report barely circulated, so there is no new official supply for the market to price.

items.title: Rumour of Chinese gold import halt rattles Shanghai traders
items.body: Traders in Shanghai circulated reports on Monday morning that China would suspend gold import quotas for banks, briefly widening the local premium. Later in the session the People's Bank of China said the reports were 'groundless' and that quotas would be issued as normal. The Shanghai premium returned to its prior level of about $8 an ounce by the close.

rationale: The rumour was officially denied within the same session and the local premium fully normalised, so Chinese import demand is unchanged.

items.title: CORRECTED - US core PCE prices rise 0.4% in August
items.body: Corrects core PCE monthly figure in first paragraph to 0.4% from 0.2%. US core PCE prices rose 0.4% in August, above the 0.2% consensus, the Commerce Department said; the year-on-year rate rose to 3.1%. Personal spending rose 0.5%.

rationale: The corrected figure is a hot beat on the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, which pushes yields and the dollar up and weighs on gold.

items.title: Israel and Hezbollah agree to ceasefire
items.body: Israel and Hezbollah agreed to a 60-day ceasefire brokered by the United States and France, officials said on 3 March. The truce took effect the following morning. This story was first published on 4 March 2027 and is republished today as part of our monthly Middle East archive digest; the ceasefire has held since.

rationale: This is archived news weeks old; its de-escalation effect was priced long ago and nothing new happened.

items.title: Opinion: Gold is heading to $6,000 and nothing can stop it
items.body: In this column, a retired fund manager argues that persistent fiscal deficits and central-bank buying will push gold to $6,000 within three years. The piece presents no new data or policy announcements. The views expressed are the author's own.

rationale: An opinion column with no new facts carries no information for the near-term price, however bullish its tone.

items.title: US inflation cools to lowest in a year
items.body: US annual CPI inflation eased to 2.7% in September from 2.9%, helped by a favourable base effect from last year's energy spike. But core prices rose 0.5% on the month, well above the 0.3% consensus, the largest monthly gain since early 2025, driven by shelter and services. Two-year Treasury yields jumped 14 basis points after the data.

rationale: The cooling headline is a base effect; the market-relevant core m/m beat sharply, front-end yields jumped, and higher real rates weigh on gold.

items.title: Retraction: no North Korean missile flew over Japan, ministry says
items.body: Japan's defence ministry retracted an alert issued an hour earlier about a North Korean ballistic missile passing over Hokkaido, saying a radar data error triggered the warning and that no launch occurred. Spot gold had jumped about $18 on the original alert. Officials apologised for the false warning.

rationale: The retraction removes the safe-haven premium added on the false alert, so the $18 spike should unwind; the effect is small and short-lived.

items.title: Fed to cut rates in December? Wexford says not without weaker jobs
items.body: Federal Reserve Governor Lena Wexford said on Friday she would not support a December rate cut unless the labour market weakens 'materially' from here, adding that recent inflation readings were 'uncomfortably firm'. She said she sees a case for holding rates for several meetings. Markets had priced a 70% chance of a December cut before her remarks.

rationale: Despite the 'Fed to cut' framing, the governor pushed back against a heavily priced cut, which lifts yields and the dollar and is bearish for gold.

items.title: Treasury yields plunge as investors seek safety
items.body: Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields rose 13 basis points to 4.71% on Tuesday, their biggest one-day gain since March, after a weak auction and hotter-than-expected producer prices. Real yields on 10-year TIPS climbed 11 basis points. The dollar index gained 0.8%.

rationale: The body contradicts the headline: nominal and real yields rose sharply and the dollar firmed, both directly bearish for non-yielding gold.

items.title: Kremlin denies rejecting ceasefire proposal
items.body: The Kremlin on Wednesday denied a report that Moscow had rejected a US-drafted ceasefire framework for Ukraine, saying the text was 'under constructive study' and that a delegation would travel to Istanbul next week. A European official said the denial signalled 'genuine interest' in a deal. European equity futures rose 0.9%.

rationale: A denial of a rejection is a step toward de-escalation, raising odds of a ceasefire and trimming gold's geopolitical premium; the step is tentative, so confidence should be modest.

items.title: Arsenal edge Inter 2-1 in Champions League
items.body: A late header gave Arsenal a 2-1 win over Inter in London on Tuesday, lifting them to the top of their group.

items.title: SmartCo unveils thinner foldable phone
items.body: SmartCo showed a foldable handset 20% thinner than its predecessor, priced at $1,499, with shipments starting next month.

items.title: City council approves new bike lanes
items.body: The council voted 9-2 to add 14 km of protected bike lanes downtown over the next two years.

items.title: US jobless claims jump to 291,000, highest since 2021
items.body: Initial jobless claims rose to 291,000 last week from 228,000, far above the 230,000 consensus, with continuing claims also climbing. Treasury yields fell 8 basis points and fed funds futures added to bets on a cut next month.

items.title: Heatwave warning issued for southern Spain
items.body: Forecasters expect temperatures above 42C in Andalusia through the weekend.

rationale: Only s4 matters: a sharp jump in jobless claims lowers yields and raises cut odds, supporting gold.

items.title: Verstappen takes pole in Monaco
items.body: Max Verstappen set the fastest lap in qualifying ahead of Sunday's race.

items.title: Kenya tea exports rise 6%
items.body: Kenya's tea export earnings rose 6% in the first half on stronger demand from Pakistan.

items.title: PBoC adds 22 tonnes of gold in October, biggest purchase in two years
items.body: China's central bank raised its gold reserves by 22 tonnes in October, its largest monthly addition in two years and far above the roughly 5-tonne monthly pace of the past year and analyst estimates.

items.title: Celebrity chef opens new restaurant in Bangkok
items.body: The 80-seat restaurant will focus on regional Thai cuisine.

rationale: k3 is a clear upside surprise in official-sector demand, which is bullish for gold; the other items are irrelevant.

items.title: US core CPI jumps 0.5% in May
items.body: US core CPI rose 0.5% m/m in May versus 0.3% expected; headline CPI rose 0.4%.

items.title: US underlying inflation surges, core up 0.6%
items.body: Core consumer prices climbed 0.6% on a rounded basis in May, the Labor Department said, against a 0.3% consensus; the unrounded gain was 0.55%.

items.title: Hot US inflation print dents rate-cut hopes
items.body: May's 0.5% core CPI gain pushed two-year yields up 15 basis points and lifted the dollar index 0.7%, as traders pared bets on a summer cut.

items.title: Tokyo marks Olympic anniversary
items.body: Tokyo held ceremonies to mark six years since it hosted the Summer Games.

items.title: Battery startup raises $200 million
items.body: A solid-state battery startup closed a $200 million funding round led by sovereign funds.

rationale: Three outlets report the same hot core CPI print (0.5-0.6% depending on rounding); yields and the dollar rose, which is bearish for gold.

items.title: US payrolls beat with 265,000 jobs
items.body: Nonfarm payrolls rose 265,000 in March against a 170,000 forecast, unemployment fell to 4.0% and wages rose 0.4%. Two-year yields rose 12 basis points.

items.title: Militia attacks two tankers in Gulf of Oman; US sends carrier group
items.body: Iran-backed fighters struck two oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman with drones, and the Pentagon ordered a carrier group to the area. Brent crude rose 4%.

items.title: Library extends weekend opening hours
items.body: The central library will open until 8 pm on Saturdays from next month.

items.title: Esports tournament sets prize-pool record
items.body: The annual tournament's prize pool reached $45 million, a new record.

rationale: p1 is bearish via higher yields while p2 is bullish via safe-haven demand; with two opposing material drivers the net direction is genuinely uncertain and confidence must stay low.

items.title: Cloud software firm prices IPO above range
items.body: The company raised $1.8 billion, valuing it at $22 billion.

items.title: England beat India in Lord's test
items.body: England won by six wickets on the final day.

items.title: Bordeaux harvest begins early
items.body: Growers began picking two weeks earlier than usual after a hot summer.

items.title: Lisbon airport strike disrupts flights
items.body: About 300 flights were cancelled as ground staff walked out for 24 hours.

items.title: Fed chair: further hikes 'on the table' if inflation persists
items.body: The Fed chair told a banking conference that further rate increases remain 'on the table' if inflation does not resume falling, and that cuts are 'not part of the discussion'. Two-year yields rose 11 basis points and the dollar index gained 0.6%.

items.title: Animated film tops weekend box office
items.body: The film took $96 million in its North American opening.

items.title: Bitcoin network hash rate hits record
items.body: Mining difficulty adjusted upward by 4% after hash rate reached a new high.

rationale: The buried item m5 is a hawkish Fed signal that lifted yields and the dollar, bearish for gold; the rest is noise.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine sign ceasefire in Istanbul
items.body: Russia and Ukraine signed a ceasefire in Istanbul taking effect at midnight along the roughly 1,200 km front line, with monitoring by an international mission.

items.title: Ukraine truce agreed; front of about 1,000 km to be frozen
items.body: Negotiators agreed to freeze fighting along a front line of about 1,000 km, according to a European diplomat, with talks on a permanent settlement to begin within 30 days.

items.title: Kyiv and Moscow agree halt to fighting; European gas prices drop 9%
items.body: European gas futures fell 9% and regional stocks rallied after the two sides agreed to stop fighting.

items.title: Bundesliga: Leverkusen held at home
items.body: Leverkusen drew 1-1 with Mainz.
